title: Put a full bottle on a top-load water cooler with both hands, turning it neck-down quickly right over the crown
instruction: Put the full bottle on the water cooler.
context: Water delivery drivers and office facilities workers swap the bottles on top-load water coolers many times a day (O*NET 53-3031.00, Driver/Sales Workers; 37-2011.00, Janitors and Cleaners). Once its cap is off, a full bottle can only be turned neck-down quickly: with both hands on it, lifted over the cooler's crown and turned in one motion right above the receptacle, so the open neck drops straight in and the bottle sits on its shoulder; what runs into the receptacle on the way is not lost. Turned over slowly, paused on its side or turned over the floor and carried neck-down, it glugs water out of the neck, and a bottle seated off center props on the crown and leaks or falls. The bottle here is wider than one hand can grip and is lifted by two clip-on bottle handles, one on each side, and suppliers tell customers to turn it with both hands.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. A top-load water cooler, scaled and shortened, is fixed on the table centered at x 20.5, y 0: a white 12 by 12 cm cabinet 9 cm tall with a red and a blue tap mark on its front face, and on top a gray crown plate with a 3.3 cm square receptacle opening that runs 3.5 cm down to a reservoir that holds 60 mL of water and takes 195 mL up to a seated neck's tip. A full 3-gallon cooler bottle at 1:2.5 scale stands upright on the table centered at x 33.5, y 0: clear blue PET with molded ribs, 10.6 cm across and 14.3 cm tall (10.5 cm body, 1.8 cm shoulder, 2 cm neck 2.2 cm across), uncapped, holding 727 mL of water, 0.80 kg in all. Two dark gray clip-on bottle handles (spring-clip carry handles of the kind sold for 3- and 5-gallon bottles) grip its sides 6.5 cm above its base, one toward each arm (y); each grip is 4 cm long, stands 4.5 cm out from the bottle and is 2.5 cm thick, and a 3.2 cm band joins their clips around the bottle. Nothing else is on the table. The water is drawn inside the bottle and as a stream when it runs out.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole run and tracks the water in mL. The open neck lets water out at 73 mL/s whenever the bottle holds more than fits below its neck at its tilt (from about 60 degrees on), straight down into the receptacle if the stream falls into it, else onto the floor as spill; a neck seated in the receptacle feeds the reservoir only until the water covers it. The score is 0, irreversibly, if the bottle falls (tipped past 45 degrees for 3 control steps with no gripper on a handle and its neck not in the receptacle) or is turned past 90 degrees with only one gripper on a handle outside the receptacle for 3 steps in all; a gripper holds a handle when its fingers are stopped by it (10 to 60 percent open) with its tool point within 1 cm of the handle. It is 0 unless the bottle ends seated: within 5 degrees of straight down, the neck's tip inside the opening (within 7.5 mm of its center line) and at least 1.5 cm below the crown, and still. Seated, it scores 0.25 if more than 73 mL (10 percent of the bottle) was ever spilled, counting water that a stream puts in the reservoir past its 195 mL air-lock level, 0.5 if a gripper still holds a handle or a tool point is within 1 cm of the bottle, and 1.0 let go with both arms home (each tool point within 3 cm of where it started) and still, 0.9 with an arm not home. Success is a full score held for 1 s. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.9, 1.0. In a real trial, weigh the bottle before and after, weigh an absorbent mat laid around the cooler for the spill, check that the bottle stands straight with its shoulder on the crown and count the hands on the bottle during the turn on the video.
reset_notes: Lift the bottle off, refill it to 727 mL, stand it back on its spot with the handles toward the arms, draw the reservoir down to 60 mL through the taps and replace the absorbent mat with a dry one.
fidelity: 1:2.5 scale of a 3-gallon bottle (0.8 kg, not 12.5 kg) with two clip-on carry handles; the cooler is cut to 9 cm tall because the arms lift only 22 cm, but its crown is to scale. No fluid simulation: a deterministic flow model lets out what does not fit below the neck at 73 mL/s, so the bottle empties in the 10 s a real one does. Water weight does not slosh and is drawn along the bottle's axis, not level, and the cooler is the open-reservoir type, with no probe to pierce a cap.
